primary_topics: Address at the Bukas Loob sa Diyos (BLD) Covenant Community event at SMX, June 15, 2013 -- invited by Rev. Fr. Anton C.T. Pascual, Brother Ding T. Sanchez and Sister Lulu E. Carrasco; compelled by Bai de los Reyes (CJP's shepherd in BLD since 1986)

The good-news-bad-news parable: a medieval farmer whose every apparent setback is met with 'Good news, bad news, who knows? I will just keep trying my best and God will do the rest' -- applied as the theological framework for CJP's own life

The most detailed account of CJP's seven JBC rejections and the two specific Scripture passages (Luke 11:1-11 and Luke 9:28-36) that confirmed his perseverance, culminating in the mysterious passage of September 13, 1995 and Ramos's question ('How did you do it?') -- answered: 'The Lord did it. Hallelujah!'

CJP's full corporate directorship portfolio named for the first time in the corpus: Meralco, PLDT, BPI, Metrobank, Petron, GMA Network, First Philippine Holdings, Jollibee, Metro Pacific Investments, Metro Pacific Tollways, Robinsons Land and Asian Terminals -- 12 blue chip companies

The BLD compulsion: invited by Fr. Anton Pascual, Bro. Ding Sanchez and Sister Lulu Carrasco; CJP generally refuses speeches; but Bai de los Reyes called Leni who handed CJP the phone; 'Bai and her late husband Sonny were our shepherds when we entered Bukas Loob sa Diyos Covenant Community in 1986... the Lord's instruments in bringing me back to Christ. So, what could I have answered her? Nothing at all, except to say Amen.'

The good-news-bad-news parable (full): farmer, wife, 20-year-old son; horse runs away (bad news); horse returns with 10 wild horses (good news); son breaks leg (bad news); kingdom goes to war, all able-bodied men conscripted except the lame son; kingdom loses war, all young men killed (good news for the farmer); farmer's response each time: 'Good news, bad news, who knows? I will just keep trying my best and God will do the rest'
Born poor: no faith, no prayer; UST Trinity failure; enrolled at FEU; Yale scholarship denied; but 'my initial frustrations and difficulties in life turned out to be blessings in disguise'

Bukas Loob sa Diyos (1986): entered the BLD Covenant Community with Leni; became renewed Catholics; read over 100 books on Bible and Catholicism; Second Plenary Council (1991); Pontifical Council for the Laity (1996-2000)

Meeting Leni: through NUSP, 'interacted with convent-bred students'; St. Scholastica's College represented by 'a lovely, sweet, thoughtful and intelligent lady, Ms Elenita A. Carpio, who after a fabled courtship agreed to be my wife and lifelong partner'

Seven JBC rejections 1992-1994: each of seven vacancies submitted to JBC; failed each time; January 1995: 'I humbled myself and bowed to what I thought was God's will for me'; prayer of surrender: 'Take oh Lord, all that I am, all that I will ever be. Take my personal ambition, my liberty, my career. Do what You will with them and I will follow whatever You want me to do'

July 1995 Luke passages: woke at 1:00 AM July 29, prayed for over two hours; Sunday July 30, serving as Special Minister of Holy Communion, heard Luke 11:1-11: 'Ask and you shall receive... whoever knocks is admitted'; had cold perspiration and goose pimples; one week later: Luke 9:28-36: 'This is my Son, my Chosen One. Listen to Him.' -- 'These three words struck me'

JBC September 13, 1995: 'there was a serious attempt to vote me out from the list'; one member pleaded for his name to remain; two weeks later, 'no one by some mysterious reason objected to my inclusion'; first time in three years CJP miraculously passed the screening
Ramos's question: 'How did you do it? How did you get the JBC to nominate you?' CJP: 'Well, sir. I did not do it. The Lord did it. Hallelujah!'

After SC: offered seats in dozen blue chip companies -- Meralco, PLDT, BPI, Metrobank, Petron, GMA Network, First Philippine Holdings, Jollibee, Metro Pacific Investments, Metro Pacific Tollways, Robinsons Land and Asian Terminals
Five arcs and To God be the glory close

When Ramos asked 'How did you do it?', the answer 'The Lord did it. Hallelujah!' is the most theologically charged statement in the entire corpus.

one_paragraph_summary: Delivered June 15, 2013 at an SMX event of the Bukas Loob sa Diyos (BLD) Covenant Community -- invited by Fr. Anton Pascual, Bro. Ding Sanchez and Sister Lulu Carrasco; accepted because BLD shepherd Bai de los Reyes called Leni and CJP could not refuse ('Bai and her late husband Sonny were our shepherds when we entered BLD in 1986... the Lord's instruments in bringing me back to Christ... what could I have answered her? Nothing at all, except to say Amen') -- this address opens with a just-returned anecdote from Czestochowa, Poland where Fr. Simon described Cardinal Tagle as 'the Karol Wojtyla of Asia.' CJP presents the good-news-bad-news parable (a medieval farmer's horse runs away, returns with ten wild horses; son breaks leg, is spared from a war that kills all able-bodied men; farmer's response each time: 'Good news, bad news, who knows? I will just keep trying my best and God will do the rest') as the governing theological framework. He applies it to his own life: the UST Trinity failure, the Yale denial, and -- most fully told -- the seven JBC rejections (1992-1994). In January 1995, after failing seven times: 'Take oh Lord, all that I am, all that I will ever be. Take my personal ambition, my liberty, my career.' On the morning of Sunday July 30, 1995, serving as Special Minister of Holy Communion, he heard Luke 11:1-11: 'Ask and you shall receive... whoever knocks is admitted' -- 'I had cold perspiration and goose pimples.' One week later: Luke 9:28-36: 'This is my Son, my Chosen One. Listen to Him.' At the JBC meeting of September 13, 1995: 'there was a serious attempt to vote me out... no one by some mysterious reason objected'; for the first time in three years, he miraculously passed. Ramos called and asked: 'How did you do it? How did you get the JBC to nominate you?' CJP's answer: 'I did not do it. The Lord did it. Hallelujah!' After Chief Justice, he lists 12 post-retirement corporate boards (Meralco, PLDT, BPI, Metrobank, Petron, GMA Network, First Philippine Holdings, Jollibee, MPIC, Metro Pacific Tollways, Robinsons Land, Asian Terminals) and closes with the five arcs and 'To God be the glory.'
